title: Skill Issue: How We Used AI to Make Agents Actually Good at Supabase — Pedro Rodrigues, Supabase
talk_summary: Pedro Rodrigues (Supabase) shows how to write agent 'skills' (skill.md + reference files + scripts, loaded via progressive disclosure) and, more importantly, how to test them: define metrics, write the skill, run eval scenarios with and without the skill, grade deterministically (tool-call/artifact assertions) or with LLM-as-judge, then iterate. He also demonstrates a real defect (Postgres view bypassing RLS without security_invoker) that a skill fixes, and candidly shows how easy it is to write a broken eval that gives inverted results.

takeaways.technique: A/B skill evals with and without the skill
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the same eval scenario twice — once with skill.md injected into the system prompt, once without — and diff the resulting artifacts to prove the skill actually changes behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to test two conditions, one with the skill and another without it

takeaways.technique: Deterministic assertions over LLM-judge where possible
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer asserting on concrete artifacts (tool called, flag present in migration, file content) rather than free-text grading; use LLM-as-judge only for non-deterministic outputs.

takeaways.technique: Beware inverted/broken evals — validate the grader
takeaways.what_they_do: He wrote an assertion that inspected the wrong thing, so 'with skill' failed and 'without skill' passed even though outputs were identical; lesson is to sanity-check the grader itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I was evaluating something wrong ... the results came a bit off

takeaways.technique: Progressive-disclosure skill files instead of fat prompts/MCP tool dumps
takeaways.what_they_do: skill.md front-matter (name + description) is always in context; body and reference files load only when the agent decides it needs them, keeping baseline context small.
takeaways.numbers: skills took ~1.3k tokens in his context vs MCP tool loading

takeaways.technique: Description wording drives skill loading; test load/no-load
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefixing the description with the verb 'use' raised load rate on Claude; he tests scenarios where the skill should and shouldn't load and tunes the description.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the verb use ... increases the chances of the skill being loaded

takeaways.technique: MCP for the mechanism, skill for the how
takeaways.what_they_do: Use MCP tools for authenticated, environment-independent actions (DB access, migrations) and skills to describe intent/workflow and chunking, rather than choosing one over the other.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tool to enable this connection, this integration, and the skill to describe how to use it
